issues.legal_issue: A charge for electricity payable under the terms of a tenancy is part of rent for determining whether the tenant has defaulted in payment of rent.
material_facts: The tenancy required payment of a monthly amount as rent and an additional monthly amount for electricity.
The tenant deposited the rent amount but did not deposit the additional electricity amount.
The landlord sought eviction on the ground of non-payment of rent.
issues.conclusion: The additional electricity charge formed part of rent under the Act, and the tenant's failure to pay it constituted default; the eviction decree was upheld and the appeal dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Although the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956 does not define rent, sections 8(3), 34 and 35 indicate that rent includes payments for amenities or services provided under the terms of a tenancy. This interpretation prevents a landlord from circumventing the Act by imposing onerous conditions for amenities as terms of the tenancy. The Court followed Karnani Properties Ltd. v. Augustin, [1957] SCR 20, and approved in part Residence Ltd. v. Surendra Mohan Banerjee, AIR 1951 Cal 126. It distinguished Radha Kishan Sao v. Gopal Modi, [1977] 2 SCC 656, because that case concerned an independent contract for furniture, unconnected with the tenancy, and a different rent law.

predicates.tenant_eviction_for_rent_default: The landlord brought a proceeding seeking the tenant's eviction on the ground of default in paying rent.
predicates.separate_charge_required_under_tenancy_f: The tenancy terms required the tenant to pay a separate charge for an amenity or service connected with the tenancy.
predicates.tenant_failed_to_pay_amenity_charge: The tenant did not pay the charge required for the amenity or service.
predicates.tenant_is_in_default_in_payment_of_rent: The tenant is in default in payment of rent.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding alleges rent default, a tenant who fails to pay a tenancy-required charge for an amenity or service is treated as being in default in payment of rent.
